cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Simple ≠ Difficult – easy to do or understand ≠ not easy to do; needing effort.

p.em: Example: The basic idea is simple and easy to understand.

cosy-blockquote.p: Quiet – with very little noise; calm.

p.em: Example: I like to read a book in a quiet room.

cosy-blockquote.p: Reduce – to make something smaller or less.

p.em: Example: We can reduce our screen time on our phones.

cosy-blockquote.p: Nature – the physical world with trees, plants, and wild animals.

p.em: Example: I love walking in nature on sunny days.

cosy-blockquote.p: Routine – your normal plan or habits for every day.

p.em: Example: Eating breakfast is part of my morning routine.

cosy-blockquote.p: Celebrate – to do something special for a fun day.

p.em: Example: We celebrate this holiday with a small family dinner.

cosy-blockquote.p: Tidy – to clean a room and put things in their correct places.

p.em: Example: You should tidy your room every weekend.

cosy-blockquote.p: Peaceful – calm, quiet, and with no stress.

p.em: Example: He found a peaceful spot in the park to rest.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hobby – an activity that you do for fun in your free time.

p.em: Example: Gardening is a very relaxing and simple hobby.

cosy-blockquote.p: Thankful – feeling or showing thanks; grateful.

p.em: Example: I am thankful for my healthy life.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
What does it mean to live a simple life, and how do you start?
★ What is one simple thing that makes you very happy?

Why is it important to spend time in a quiet place, and what does it change?
★ Where do you go when you want a quiet moment?

How do we reduce our monthly expenses easily?
★ What monthly expense did you reduce recently?

Why do people feel more relaxed when they are in nature?
★ How often do you walk in a forest or park?

What is your morning routine and how does it help you?
★ Is your daily routine busy or relaxed?

How does your family celebrate traditional holidays?
★ How did you celebrate your last birthday?

Why does it feel satisfying when you tidy your wardrobe?
★ Do you need to tidy your bedroom desk today?

What makes a neighborhood feel peaceful and calm?
★ Is your current neighborhood peaceful or noisy?

Does a physical hobby feel better than a digital one?
★ What hobbies do you practice in your free time?

Why do we feel thankful for simple things like fresh coffee?
★ What simple thing are you most thankful for today?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: 🌀 Activity 1: Minimalist Desk vs Cluttered Desk Where do you work best? Together with your partner, compare these two physical workspaces. Talk about what is on each desk. Practice using the Simple Present tense (I see..., I prefer...): 📅 📅 The Perfect Plan (Minimalist) Only a single laptop, a glass of water, and absolute quiet focus. 🌀 🌀 The Happy Accident (Cluttered) Filled with colorful markers, notebooks, coffee cups, and spontaneous ideas. 🍃 Closing: A Quiet Walk If you could spend one entire day doing only simple, quiet things in nature today, which peaceful activity would you choose? 🌲 Walking silently in a deep forest 🍎 Preparing a fresh home-cooked meal 📖 Reading a real paper book under a tree 🎨 Painting a simple flower with watercolors

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, will we reduce our screen time because we are always online?
★ Do you reduce your phone use on weekends?

Will smart homes do all our physical chores so we lose our simple daily routine?
★ Do you find doing simple tasks like washing dishes to be a good daily routine?

Will governments ask us to pay a tax if we do not live a simple life?
★ Do you think a simple life with only 100 personal possessions is possible?

As big cities grow, will quiet nature become too expensive for normal people?
★ Do you like quiet weekends in nature?

Will traditional hobbies like gardening disappear because of computer games?
★ Do you prefer real hobbies to video games?

Will we celebrate free time more than a busy job?
★ Do you want more free time or more money?

Will we live in tiny, clean micro-homes that are easy to tidy?
★ Do you want to live in a small, tidy home?

In the future, will we feel thankful for simple things only when they are expensive?
★ Are you happy when you buy simple things?

Will future schools teach children how to live a peaceful and happy life?
★ Was your childhood peaceful?

Will people leave big cities to find a quiet and simple life in country villages?
★ Do you want to live in a quiet country house?

ul.li: Incorrect: I prefer a life more simple → Correct: I prefer a simpler life ((Comparative form of 'simple' is 'simpler'))
Incorrect: I am work in a peaceful place → Correct: I work in a peaceful place ((Simple present structure))
Incorrect: She tidies always her room → Correct: She always tidies her room ((Adverbs of frequency come before the main verb))
